Artifacts.name: Antikythera Mechanism
Artifacts.historicalContext: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek hand-powered astronomical calculator. It is widely described as the oldest known example of an analog computer, used to predict astronomical positions and eclipses for calendar and astrological purposes decades in advance.

Artifacts.name: Excalibur Sword
Artifacts.historicalContext: Excalibur is the legendary sword of King Arthur, said to possess magical properties and signify the rightful sovereignty of Great Britain. According to myth, it was given to Arthur by the Lady of the Lake and later returned to her waters upon his death.

Artifacts.name: Rosetta Stone
Artifacts.historicalContext: The Rosetta Stone is a granodiorite stele inscribed with three versions of a decree issued in Memphis, Egypt, in 196 BC. The top and middle texts are in Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic and Demotic scripts respectively, while the bottom is in Ancient Greek. It provided the key to modern translation of Egyptian hieroglyphs.

Artifacts.name: Codex Gigas (Devil's Bible)
Artifacts.historicalContext: The Codex Gigas is the largest extant medieval manuscript in the world, created in the early 13th century in the Benedictine monastery of Podlažice in Bohemia. It contains the complete Vulgate Bible as well as historical documents, all written in Latin. It is famous for its full-page portrait of the devil.

Artifacts.name: Rosetta Stone
Artifacts.historicalContext: The Rosetta Stone is one of the most important historical artifacts in the world. It contains the same decree written in three different scripts: Ancient Greek, Demotic, and Egyptian hieroglyphs. Its discovery played a crucial role in helping scholars decode ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs and greatly improved our understanding of Ancient Egyptian civilization.
Artifacts.presentLocation: The British Museum, London, United Kingdom

Artifacts.name: Antikythera Mechanism
Artifacts.historicalContext: The Antikythera Mechanism is an ancient Greek mechanical device believed to have been used to calculate and display astronomical cycles. Its complex system of gears demonstrates an advanced understanding of mathematics, astronomy, and mechanical engineering in the ancient world. It is often regarded as one of the earliest known analog computing devices.
